Avodah Zarah 71b:11.english: The Gemara cites a claim against Rav Ashi’s opinion that a gentile cannot acquire an item by pulling it: Mar Kashisha, son of Rav Ḥisda, said to Rav Ashi: Come and hear an objection to your opinion from the mishna: In the case of a Jew who sells his wine to a gentile, if the Jew fixed a price before he measured the wine into the gentile’s vessel, deriving benefit from the money paid for the wine is permitted, as the wine was acquired by the gentile before the gentile touched it. And if you say that pulling an item does not acquire it in a transaction involving a gentile, why is the money paid for it permitted? Rav Ashi replied: Here we are dealing with a case where the gentile paid the Jew a dinar in advance, before the measuring, thereby acquiring the wine with money.

Avodah Zarah 71b:12.english: One of the Sages raised an objection: If that is so, say the last clause: But if the Jew measured the wine into the gentile’s vessel, thereby rendering it forbidden, before the Jew fixed a price, the money paid for the wine is forbidden. And if the gentile paid the Jew a dinar in advance, why should the money paid for it be forbidden?

Avodah Zarah 71b:13.english: Rav Ashi said to Mar Kashisha: And according to you, Mar Kashisha, as you say that pulling acquires items in a transaction involving a gentile, why in the first clause is the money paid for it permitted, and in the latter clause the money paid for it is forbidden?

Avodah Zarah 71b:14.english: Rather, what do you, Mar Kashisha, have to say to explain the distinction between the two cases? You, Mar Kashisha, say that when the Jew fixed a price, the gentile consequently relied on the Jew that the sale would not be canceled, and so the sale was concluded by the pulling. But in a case where the Jew did not fix a price, the gentile did not rely on the Jew that the sale would not be canceled, and therefore the sale was not concluded.

Avodah Zarah 71b:15.english: According to Rav Ashi's opinion as well, even though the gentile gave the Jew a dinar in advance, if the Jew fixed a price, the gentile relied on the Jew that the sale would not be canceled, and if the Jew did not fix a price, the gentile did not rely on the Jew that the sale would not be canceled.

Avodah Zarah 71b:16.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi: Come and hear another proof against Rav Ashi's opinion, as Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba says that Rabbi Yoḥanan says: A descendant of Noah, i.e., a gentile, is executed by the court for theft of even less than the value of one peruta; but if the gentile stole less than the value of one peruta from a Jew, the gentile is not subject to restitution, i.e., the gentile is not obligated to return it, as the Jew presumably waived the debt. And if you say that pulling an item does not acquire it in a transaction involving a gentile, why should the gentile be executed? The gentile did not commit a legally significant act by stealing the item, as it remains in the possession of the owner.

Avodah Zarah 71b:17.english: The Gemara answers: The gentile is executed because the gentile caused a Jew distress by stealing the item, even though by the halakhot of acquisition the thief did not acquire it.

Avodah Zarah 72a:2.english: The Gemara asks: If that is so, say the latter clause of that halakhic statement: If another descendant of Noah came and took the stolen item from the first gentile, the second gentile is also executed for it. Granted, with regard to the first clause it can be explained that although there is no obligation to return the item, the gentile is executed because the first gentile caused the Jew distress; but with regard to the latter clause, what did the second gentile do? The second gentile did not cause the Jew distress, and since the item is worth less than one peruta, one is not obligated to return it unless the second gentile stole it from a gentile. Consequently, the second theft should not be considered a legally significant act.

Avodah Zarah 72a:3.english: Rather, should one not conclude from it that a gentile pulling an item acquires it in a transaction performed by a gentile? Accordingly, the actions of both the first and second gentiles are legally significant acts of theft, for which the gentiles are liable to be executed. The Gemara affirms: Conclude from it that this is so.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:11:1.hebrew: פסק עד שלא מדד דמיו מותרין - דכי מדד קניה עובד כוכבים במשיכה וקמו זוזי בהלואה גביה, יין נסך לא הוי עד דנגע ביה:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:11:2.english: that he paid him a dinar in advance - that the gentile gave the Jew his money beforehand.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:12:1.hebrew:
שהקדים לו - ונתן לו מעות יותר מכדי דמי היין עד שיפסוק הדמים, יחזיר לו ישראל את המותר:
אמאי דמיו אסורין:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:13:1.hebrew: ולדידך דאמרת - טעמא דרישא משום דמשיכה קונה, סיפא נמי אמאי דמיו אסורין:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:14:1.english: his mind was at rest - the gentile's mind was at rest to acquire through pulling.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:14:2.hebrew: לא פסק - קודם משיכה לא סמכא דעתיה למקנייה במשיכה, שמא ירבה לו בדמיו:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:16:1.hebrew: בן נח - שגזל את ישראל פחות משוה פרוטה, אע"ג דגבי ישראל לאו ממונא הוא דמחלי עליה, גבי עובד כוכבים ממונא הוא. ובן נח נצטוה על הגזל בסנהדרין (דף נו.), ואזהרה שלהן זו היא מיתתן ואין צריכין התראה:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:16:2.hebrew: ולא ניתן להישבון - ולא מחייב לאהדורה להאי ישראל, דהא מחיל עליה:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:16:3.hebrew: אמאי נהרג - הא לא קניא להך גזילה, וכל היכא דאיתא של ישראל היא:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 71b:17:1.english: And it answers that this gentile is executed because of the distress of the Jew.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 72a:1:1.hebrew: ומאי לא ניתן להישבון - הא לא שייך ביה הישבון, דכיון דעובד כוכבים לא קנייה דישראל היא:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 72a:1:2.hebrew: אינה בתורת הישבון - כלומר, ה"נ קאמר: אינה בתורת שום גזילה דעובד כוכבים, דכל היכא דאיתא דמרה היא. וה"ה לשוה פרוטה, והאי דנקט פחות לאשמועינן דנהרג עליה:

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 72a:3:1.hebrew: אלא שמע מינה משיכה קונה - הלכך קניה קמא, והדר קניה האי, ונהרג על שגזל. ולא ניתן להישבון דרישא דוקא פחות משוה פרוטה, דישראל מחיל ולא מיחייב עובד כוכבים לאהדורה:

Shulchan Arukh, Yoreh De'ah 132:2.english:
When an Israelite has sold his wine to a pagan, he can benefit from the money received if the wine has not yet been delivered, because the wine is forbidden only from the moment the pagan has touched it, which he could not do before delivery. But if the pagan took the wine before the definitive conclusion of the market, it is forbidden for the Israelite to benefit from the money received; the pagan having touched the wine before payment, this sale is assimilated to that of wine intended for idols.
GLOSE: As soon as the wine belongs to the pagan, the Israelite no longer has any right to supervise the liquid, and there is reason to fear then that the idolater may have touched it. It is only a question here of the case where the Israelite measured the wine in his own vessel or in that of the pagan which has no impediment. But if the Israelite measured the liquid in the pagan's vessel equipped with a device that can slow down the transfer of wine, or in his own vessel held and agitated by the pagan to facilitate the flow of wine, if the Israelite wants in this case to benefit from the price of his merchandise, he must receive the money before measuring the wine, whether the pagan shakes the vessel left on the ground, or takes it in his hands. However, if the Israelite measured the wine in the vessel belonging to the pagan, and carrying a device that allowed a small part of the liquid poured first by the pagan to remain in the vessel, a mixture was formed in which the pagan's liquid renders forbidden the wine subsequently poured by the Israelite; however, in case of accomplished fact, it is permitted to benefit from all the wine poured into the vessel, less a quantity equal to that of the liquid belonging to the pagan and which had remained in the container. But, deliberately, the pagan's wine renders forbidden that of the Israelite when the liquid belonging to the pagan is in the vessel itself but if it is on the rim, whether the vessel is in the pagan's courtyard or in the hands of its owner, or if the Israelite, the wine being in his courtyard, asks the pagan to sell him his vessel, then the wine that the Israelite pours into the vessel is permitted, because it belongs to him as soon as it has touched the liquid on the rim of the container. Similarly, if the pagan, while the Israelite measures wine for him, lifted the vessel to show that it belongs to him, the wine is permitted, because the pagan touched it before it was measured: but if the pagan did not lift the vessel containing the wine that the Israelite was to measure, the same law applies to this liquid as to any other wine coming from a pagan. These laws were in force at the time when pagans offered wine to idols; but as in our days, there are no more pagans, it is always permitted to benefit from a wine touched by a pagan who does not practice his religion. Such is the usage generally adopted and these laws are no longer applied.

Steinsaltz comment #1 on Avodah Zarah 72.english: Rashi explains that according to this opinion, this ruling does not apply only to theft of less than the value of one peruta, as presumed in the question. Rather, this is a general statement with regard to any theft of a Noahide, even one involving more than the value of one peruta, and is stating that since the gentile does not acquire the stolen item by pulling it, the halakhot of theft and restitution do not apply. The Ra’avad explains this means that since the gentile is liable to receive the death penalty only due to the fact that the theft caused pain to a Jew, and not because he actually acquired the stolen item, therefore, restitution of the theft does not remedy the matter, although the gentile is certainly obligated to return the item to its owner (see Ritva).

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 71b:11.english: And now they bring proofs against the opinion of Rav Ashi, who holds that a gentile does not acquire through pulling. Mar Kashisha, son of Rav Ḥisda, said to Rav Ashi: Come and hear a proof from our mishna, which we learned: One who sells his wine to a gentile, if the Jew fixed its price before he measured — its money is permitted, since the wine was already acquired by the gentile before the gentile touched it. And if you say that pulling does not acquire for a gentile, why is its money permitted? Rav Ashi replied: Here, what are we dealing with? That the gentile paid the Jew a dinar in advance on account, before the measuring, and thereby acquired the wine with money.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 71b:12.english: And they object: If that is so, that it is dealing with a case where the gentile paid the Jew in advance, say the last clause of the mishna: The Jew measured before he fixed a price — its money is forbidden; and if the gentile paid the Jew a dinar in advance, why is its money forbidden?

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 71b:13.english: Rav Ashi said to Mar Kashisha: And according to your opinion that you say that pulling acquires for a gentile, why in the beginning is its money permitted, and in the end its money is forbidden?

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 71b:14.english: Rather, what do you, Mar Kashisha, have to say that you distinguish between the matters? That you, Mar Kashisha, say thus: When the Jew fixes a price — the gentile's mind relies that the sale will not be canceled, and therefore the sale is concluded by pulling, but when the Jew does not fix a price — the gentile's mind does not rely on it.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 71b:15.english: According to my opinion as well, even though the gentile paid the Jew a dinar in advance, if the Jew fixes a price for the gentile — the gentile's mind relies, if the Jew does not fix a price — the gentile's mind does not rely.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 71b:16.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi: Come and hear an additional proof against Rav Ashi's opinion, that Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said: A descendant of Noah is executed for theft of less than the value of a *peruta*, and however, for such a theft which is less than the value of a *peruta*, if the gentile stole from a Jew — the gentile is not subject to restitution, the gentile is not obligated to return it to the Jew, since the Jew does not care about it. And if you say that pulling does not acquire for a gentile, why is the gentile executed? The gentile did not do anything by stealing an object, for the object remained the property of its original owners!

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 71b:17.english: And they answer: Because the gentile caused distress to a Jew by this taking, that the gentile took property that is not the gentile's, even though from the perspective of the laws of acquisition the gentile did not acquire it.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 72a:1.english: And what does it mean that the stolen object is not subject to restitution? It means that it is not subject to the halakhot of restitution, it is not included in the law of returning stolen property, because in truth the gentile did not steal the object.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 72a:2.english: And they object: If that is so, that Rav Ashi explains, say the last clause of this *halakha*: A gentile who stole from a Jew, and his friend who is also a gentile came and took it from the first gentile — the second gentile is executed for it. Granted, in the first *halakha* Rav Ashi explains because the first gentile caused distress to a Jew, but in the last clause, what did the second one do?

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 72a:3.english: Rather, learn from here that pulling acquires for a gentile, and therefore the first gentile acquired the stolen item, and for this reason the second gentile who stole it from the first gentile is also liable. And they conclude: Indeed, learn from here that it is so.

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 71b:16:1.hebrew: בן נח נהרג על פחות משוה פרוטה - ובן נח מצווה על הגזל, ואזהרתן זו מיתתן. ולא ניתן להשבון: ודוקא ישראל דבר מחילה הוא, אבל עובד כוכבים לאו בר מחילה הוא. ורש"י פירוש דלא ניתן להשבון משום דקם ליה בדרבה מיניה, ולא נראה דא"כ לא יתחייב עובד כוכבים לשלם גזלו בשום ענין:

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 71b:16:2.hebrew: ואי ס"ד משיכה בעובד כוכבים אינה קונה, אמאי נהרג - (פירוש): הא לא קניה, וכל היכא דאיתיה ברשותיה דישראל הוא. ותימה: הרי ישראל נמי לא קנה הגזילה להיות שלו, ואפ"ה קנייה להתחייב באונסין, החיוב דשייך ביה. וה"נ יש לנו לומר בבן נח שקנאו להתחייב בה מיתה, דהיינו החיוב דשייך בה. וי"ל דודאי: אי גזל שוה פרוטה, דהוי ממונא לגבי ישראל וחיסרו, אית לן למימר כדפרישנא. אבל פחות משוה פרוטה, שלא חיסר הישראל דלאו ממונא הוא, וגם ממון העובד כוכבים לא נתרבה שהרי לא קנאה, משום הכי פריך אמאי נהרג. ומשני: צערא דישראל [ועי' תוס' עירובין סב. ד"ה בן נח וכו' ביתר ביאור]:

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 72a:1:1.hebrew: ומאי לא ניתן להישבון - פירוש: דלא שייך ביה הישבון, וכל היכא דאיתיה ברשותיה דישראל איתיה. ותימה: הרי ישראל נמי לא קנה הגזילה להיות שלו, ואפ"ה איתיה בתורת הישבון, דכתיב: והשיב הגזילה! ונראה דה"פ: מאחר שאין חיוב בה רק משום צערא דישראל, אמאי הוצרך לומר "ולא ניתן להישבון"? פשיטא, וליכא מאן דאמר שתהא השבה שייכא ביה! וא"ת: למאי דפרשי' לעיל דקאמר דמשיכה קונה בעובד כוכבים לכולי עלמא היכא דליכא זוזי, כגון במציאה ובמתנה, מאי פריך ומאי מייתי ראיה מגזל למקח וממכר? וי"ל דס"ל דאי אינה קונה בעובד כוכבים במקח, אף בגזל נמי לא תקנה, דלא דמיא למציאה ומתנה דבהיתירא אתי לידיה, אבל גזל דבאיסורא אתי לידיה, אי לא מהני משיכה במקח, לא מהני אף בגזל:
